question: After the readiness RFC is accepted, should OpenClaw standardize these four profiles with an implicit `local` report, activation identity, and release-blocking packaged conformance?
rationale: The RFC is technically coherent, but choosing supported deployment postures, defaults, security baselines, and permanent release obligations is product policy that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Stage full acceptance
options.body: Keep the RFC draft until readiness lands, then accept the four-profile contract after security, upgrade, ownership, and packaged-conformance evidence is refreshed.

options.title: Narrow the initial catalog
options.body: Accept `local` and `container` first while deferring `reverse-proxy`, `node-mode`, activation identity, or release blocking to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Retain explicit readiness only
options.body: Decline named standard profiles and let operators compose the accepted readiness criteria directly without a core-owned catalog.

recommendation.title: Stage full acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC draft until readiness lands, then accept the four-profile contract after security, upgrade, ownership, and packaged-conformance evidence is refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available organization-member routing candidate connected to adjacent profile-contract design, while release and gateway owners should also participate.
